I'm going to assume its been postulated before, yet nonetheless, I want commentary. When energy is made to flow by magnetic induction, the discharge over a gap appears as reddish, orange, and is usually hot. The discharge from a dielectric material is often blue, purple, and this coloring is often associated with "cold electricity". From my understanding I have yet to divulge anything new about this relationship. The theory I put forwards is that the REASON these discharges are colored this way has to do with the conditioning of space as it becomes polarized by the discharge.
